mainTopic: The latest time for the evening קריאת שמע and for eating the קרבן פסח: חצות, dawn, and fences of the חכמים
overview: The עמוד opens by finishing an answer: the time between dawn and sunrise is really day, and it is called 'night' only because people are still asleep. רבי יהושע בן לוי is quoted as ruling like רבי שמעון, but רב יצחק בר יוסף reports that this was only inferred from a story where he allowed it בשעת הדחק, in an emergency. The גמרא then explains the משנה about רבן גמליאל's sons: the חכמים agree that קריאת שמע may be read until dawn, and their deadline of חצות is only a fence to keep people from sin. Next, the גמרא notices that eating the קרבן פסח is missing from the משנה's list of מצוות that last until dawn, and it brings a ברייתא that does include it. רב יוסף answers that this is a מחלוקת between רבי אלעזר בן עזריה (until חצות, from the words 'בלילה הזה') and רבי עקיבא (until dawn, from the word 'בחפזון'). The גמרא then works out how each of them reads the words of the פסוקים, and shows the same argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע. רבי אבא adds that both sides agree the גאולה began at night and the leaving happened by day, and that they argue only about whose 'haste' the פסוק means. The עמוד ends with an אגדה: ה׳ asked politely, with the word נא, that ישראל borrow silver and gold from מצרים, and the reason continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The time before sunrise is really day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the time between dawn and sunrise is truly day. It is called 'night' only because people are still sleeping then.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Really it is day. The reason it is called 'night' is that there are people who sleep at that hour.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the earlier question. The ברייתא seemed to call the time after dawn 'night,' but the גמרא says it is actually day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא spoke of reading שמע twice 'at night,' once before dawn and once after dawn. That seemed to show the time after dawn counts as night. The answer is that it is legally day. The word 'night' only describes the fact that people are still lying in bed, which connects to the words 'ובשכבך,' when you lie down.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (opens the true answer)
Day
Night
People
They sleep

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the time after dawn is night. It is day. It is only called 'night' because people are still asleep. That is why רבי שמעון can treat it as part of 'ובשכבך.'

phrases.english: No, really it is day,
and the fact that they call it 'night'
is because there are people who sleep at that hour.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question on the previous amud about whether the time after dawn is night.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a word in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא calls the time after dawn 'night,' so it must be night in legal terms.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is legally day. The word 'night' just reflects that people are still sleeping then.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחא ברבי חנינא quotes רבי יהושע בן לוי as ruling like רבי שמעון in the name of רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אחא son of רבי חנינא said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון, who said it in the name of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a practical ruling. You may follow רבי שמעון and read the evening שמע after dawn, before sunrise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the גמרא only explained רבי שמעון's view. Now an אמורא says this is the actual הלכה. This ruling will soon be questioned in step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: The final ruling follows ...
In the name of

phrases.english: Rabbi Aḥa son of Rabbi Ḥanina said
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Shimon
who said it in the name of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַחָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining רבי שמעון's view, the גמרא now gives a practical ruling that follows it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may read the evening קריאת שמע after dawn and before sunrise, like רבי שמעון.

steps.title: But do not say השכיבנו
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא limits the ruling. One who reads the evening שמע after dawn should not say the ברכה of השכיבנו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: As long as he does not say 'השכיבנו' (Help us lie down).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא adds a limit to the ruling. You may read שמע then, but you skip the ברכה of השכיבנו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: השכיבנו is a prayer to lie down and sleep in peace. Since this time is really day, as step 1 showed, that prayer does not fit. So the שמע may be read, but this night ברכה is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: As long as / on condition that
The evening ברכה asking G-d to let us lie down in peace

steps.whyThisMatters: This ties back to step 1. Because the time is really day, a ברכה about going to sleep cannot be said.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
As long as he does not say 'Hashkivenu.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יֹאמַר ״הַשְׁכִּיבֵנוּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to how the ruling in step 2 is carried out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When reading the evening שמע after dawn, one leaves out השכיבנו.

steps.title: The ruling was only inferred, not said directly
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר יוסף reports that רבי יהושע בן לוי never said this ruling outright. It was only inferred from something he did.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב יצחק בר יוסף came, he said: That statement which רבי אחא ברבי חנינא said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי was not said explicitly. Rather, it was said by inference.
steps.whatsHappening: A scholar arrives from ארץ ישראל and corrects the report in step 2. רבי יהושע בן לוי did not actually say 'the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shrinks the ruling from step 2. People drew a general rule out of a single case. The next steps show what that case was, and that it was really only an emergency allowance.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
Explicitly
By inference / implied from something else
It was said / stated

steps.confusionAlert: רב יצחק בר יוסף does not say רבי שמעון's view is wrong. He only says רבי יהושע בן לוי never gave a general ruling in his favor.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף, אֲמַר:
phrases.english: When Rav Yitzḥak bar Yosef came, he said:
That which Rabbi Aḥa son of Rabbi Ḥanina
said in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi
was not stated explicitly,
rather, it was stated by inference.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו בְּפֵירוּשׁ אִיתְּמַר, אֶלָּא מִכְּלָלָא אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how step 2 was passed on and says it was not a direct statement.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects that רבי יהושע בן לוי gave a direct, general ruling like רבי שמעון.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A general rule was drawn from one specific case.

steps.title: The story of the two Sages at the wedding
steps.stepSummary: Two Sages got drunk at the wedding of רבי יהושע בן לוי's son and came to him with a question.
steps.simpleTranslation: For there was a pair of Sages who got drunk at the wedding feast of רבי יהושע בן לוי's son. They came before רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts telling the story that the ruling was inferred from. This step sets up the case for רבי יהושע בן לוי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Sages were drunk and fell asleep, so they missed the evening שמע until after dawn. That makes their situation an unusual, pressured one. This detail is what limits the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: A pair of Sages
They became drunk
Wedding feast
Before him

phrases.english: For there was a certain pair of Sages
who got drunk at the wedding feast
of the son of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi.

phrases.aramaic: אֲתוֹ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי,
phrases.english: They came before Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the story behind the inference mentioned in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The case: Sages who missed the evening שמע because they were drunk ask what to do after dawn.

steps.title: רבי שמעון may be relied on only in an emergency
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי answered that רבי שמעון is worthy to rely on בשעת הדחק. This means his view is not the הלכה in ordinary cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: רבי שמעון is worthy to rely on in a time of pressing need.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי allows the Sages to read the evening שמע after dawn. He bases this only on the fact that it is an emergency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'כדאי לסמוך עליו בשעת הדחק' show that רבי שמעון's view is only a fallback. Step 2 turned this into a general rule. In truth, you may only rely on it when you have no other choice.

keyTerms.meaning: He is worthy / it is reasonable
To rely on him
In a time of pressing need / emergency

steps.whatToRemember: In ordinary cases, the evening שמע must be read before dawn. Only בשעת הדחק may one rely on רבי שמעון and read it after dawn, before sunrise, and even then without השכיבנו.
steps.whyThisMatters: The phrase 'כדאי הוא לסמוך עליו בשעת הדחק' became a basic idea in פסק הלכה. A minority opinion may be relied on when there is real need.

phrases.english: He said: Rabbi Shimon is worthy
to rely on in a time of pressing need.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדַאי הוּא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לִסְמוֹךְ עָלָיו בִּשְׁעַת הַדְּחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יהושע בן לוי's answer to the case in step 5, proving the point of step 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהושע בן לוי did not rule like רבי שמעון in general. He only allowed relying on him בשעת הדחק.

steps.title: Quoting the story of רבן גמליאל's sons from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the opening words of the story in the משנה about רבן גמליאל's sons returning from a wedding.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'There was an incident where his sons came,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a line from the משנה so it can discuss it. This is a setup line that prepares the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבן גמליאל's sons came home from a wedding after חצות and said they had not yet read קריאת שמע. He told them that if dawn has not yet come, they are still obligated to read it. The word וכו׳ means 'and so on' and points to the rest of the story without writing it out.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident or story, usually brought as a practical example of the law
His sons, meaning the sons of רבן גמליאל
'And so on.' The quote continues, but only the opening words are written

phrases.english: The incident where his sons came, etc.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה. The sons came back late from a wedding hall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the discussion of רבי שמעון and בשעת הדחק, the גמרא turns to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the story: the sons asked whether they could still read קריאת שמע after חצות.

steps.title: Didn't the sons already know their father's opinion?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised that the sons needed to ask, since they surely knew רבן גמליאל's view that קריאת שמע may be read all night.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until now, had they not heard this ruling of רבן גמליאל?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a sharp question about the story: why did the sons need to ask their own father something he clearly held?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל's opinion in the משנה is that the evening שמע may be read until dawn. His own sons would surely have known this. So their question seems pointless, and the גמרא demands an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Until now
They had not heard

phrases.english: And until now,
had they not heard
this ruling of Rabban Gamliel?!
phrases.notes: His view that the evening שמע may be read until dawn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the story quoted in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The story in the משנה, where the sons ask their father whether they may still read קריאת שמע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The sons must have known their father's well-known opinion, so the question seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The sons were really asking about the opinion of the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: The sons were asking whether the חכמים truly disagree with רבן גמליאל, which would make the הלכה follow the majority, or whether the חכמים agree and only set חצות as a protective fence.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what they said to him: Do the חכמים disagree with you? If so, when one Sage argues against many, the הלכה follows the many. Or perhaps the חכמים hold like you, and when they say 'until חצות' it is only to keep a person away from sin?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by explaining that the sons knew their father's view. They were asking how the חכמים fit in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the חכמים truly hold that the deadline is חצות, then the rule of יחיד ורבים הלכה כרבים applies, and the sons would have missed the deadline. If instead the חכמים also hold that the real deadline is dawn, and said חצות only as an early safety deadline, then everyone agrees the sons can still read שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: They disagree with you
When one Sage argues against many, the הלכה follows the many
Or perhaps
Midnight
To keep a person far from sin, meaning a protective fence

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים's 'until חצות' does not have to be the true biblical deadline. It may be an earlier safety deadline so that people do not push off קריאת שמע and end up missing it completely.

phrases.english: This is what they said to him:
phrases.notes: This phrase introduces the reframing of the sons' question.

phrases.english: Do the Rabbis disagree with you?
If so, between one and many, the halakha follows the many.
phrases.notes: In that case, we would have to follow the חכמים.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִּלְמָא רַבָּנַן כְּווֹתָךְ סְבִירָא לְהוּ,
phrases.english: Or perhaps the Rabbis hold like you,
and that which they say 'until midnight'
is in order to distance a person from transgression?
phrases.notes: An early deadline so that people do not delay and miss the מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8 by explaining what the sons were really asking.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the question: the sons were asking about the חכמים's view, not their father's.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sons did not know their father's opinion.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sons knew his opinion. They wanted to know whether the חכמים truly argue with him or only made a protective fence.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל: the חכמים agree with me, so you are still obligated
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל answers that the חכמים agree that the real deadline is dawn. Their 'until חצות' is only a protective fence, so his sons must still read שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: The חכמים hold like me, and you are obligated. When they say 'until חצות,' it is only to keep a person away from sin.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל answers his sons' real question. The חכמים do not truly disagree with him, so the sons must read קריאת שמע now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no real dispute between one Sage and many, so the majority rule does not come into play. The חכמים's חצות is an early safety deadline. After the fact, even the חכמים agree that one can and must read שמע until dawn.

keyTerms.meaning: They hold like me
You are obligated

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים's deadline of חצות is a fence to keep people from delaying. The true time for the evening שמע lasts until dawn, so someone who is late must still read it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the whole מחלוקת in the משנה: רבן גמליאל and the חכמים agree about the real deadline. They differ only about the protective fence.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לְהוּ: רַבָּנָן כְּווֹתִי סְבִירָא לְהוּ,
phrases.english: He said to them: The Rabbis hold like me,
and you are obligated.
phrases.notes: You must still read שמע now.

phrases.english: And that which they say 'until midnight'
is in order to distance a person from transgression.
phrases.notes: The words repeat the sons' question, now confirmed as the correct option.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְהוּ: רַבָּנָן כְּווֹתִי סְבִירָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the two-sided question the sons asked in step 9 by choosing the second option.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do the חכמים truly disagree with רבן גמליאל, or is their חצות only a fence?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים agree with him. חצות is only a fence, so the sons are still obligated.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Even according to the חכמים, the evening שמע may be read after the fact until dawn.

steps.title: Quoting the next line: this rule applies beyond קריאת שמע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, where רבן גמליאל says this is not the only case. Wherever the חכמים said 'until חצות,' the מצוה may be done until dawn.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And not only this did they say, but rather,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה to begin discussing it. This is a setup line for the next part of the סוגיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבן גמליאל widens the principle. Every time the חכמים set a deadline of חצות, the real deadline is dawn, and חצות is only a fence. The גמרא is about to examine this line.

keyTerms.meaning: And not only this
But rather

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא זוֹ בִּלְבַד אָמְרוּ, אֶלָּא וְכוּ׳:
phrases.english: And not only this did they say, but rather, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה continues: wherever the חכמים said 'until חצות,' the מצוה may be done until dawn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the story of the sons, the גמרא moves to the משנה's broader principle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces the principle that every 'until חצות' of the חכמים really extends until dawn.

steps.title: Does רבן גמליאל really say 'until midnight'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבן גמליאל uses wording that sounds like he agrees to the 'until חצות' deadline.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבן גמליאל hold 'until חצות'? Then why does the משנה have him say 'And not only this did they say'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of רבן גמליאל's statement in the משנה. His words make it sound like he accepts the 'until חצות' rule, which is not his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל holds that the deadline is dawn, not חצות. Yet 'not only this did they say,' followed by a list of 'until חצות' cases, sounds like he is building on the חצות rule. The גמרא wants to know why he would talk as if 'until חצות' were his own position.

keyTerms.meaning: Does he say? (a challenge question, expecting 'no')
that the text teaches / that it says
And not only this did they say (the opening of רבן גמליאל's list in the משנה)

phrases.english: But does Rabban Gamliel say 'until midnight'?
phrases.notes: He holds that the deadline is dawn.

phrases.english: That it teaches: 'And not only this did they say'?
phrases.notes: This wording sounds like he is adding to a 'until midnight' rule.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מִי קָאָמַר עַד חֲצוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the משנה line quoted in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'וְלֹא זוֹ בִּלְבַד אָמְרוּ' in רבן גמליאל's statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבן גמליאל holds the deadline is dawn. So he should not speak as if he accepts and extends a 'until חצות' rule.

steps.title: He was explaining the Rabbis' view to his sons
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל was telling his sons that even the חכמים, who say 'until חצות', agree that the real deadline is dawn. Their חצות is only a fence against sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבן גמליאל meant to tell his sons: Even according to the חכמים, who say 'until חצות', the מצוה really lasts until dawn. When they say 'until חצות', it is only to keep a person far away from sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רבן גמליאל was not stating his own view. He was describing the חכמים' view and showing that even they agree the real deadline is dawn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'not only this did they say' is about the חכמים' rulings, not his own. He is showing that every 'until חצות' rule of the חכמים is really a dawn deadline with an added safety fence. So the wording fits his view after all.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he meant (introduces a reinterpretation)
its מצוה, the real obligation
to distance a person from sin (the reason for a protective fence)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the חכמים hold that the מצוה truly ends at חצות. According to this answer, they agree it lasts until dawn. חצות is only an earlier deadline they set as a safety measure.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key idea: many rabbinic deadlines are fences placed before the actual תורה deadline. They are not the actual תורה deadline itself.

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי קָאָמַר לְהוּ רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לִבְנֵיהּ:
phrases.english: This is what Rabban Gamliel said to his sons:
Even according to the Rabbis, who say 'until midnight,'
its מצוה lasts until dawn rises.
And the fact that they say 'until midnight'
is in order to distance a person from transgression.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר לְהוּ רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לִבְנֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבן גמליאל seemed to be stating and extending a 'until חצות' rule as his own.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was describing the חכמים' rulings. He showed that even for them the real deadline is dawn, and חצות is only a fence.

steps.title: Quoting the next case: burning fats on the altar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next item in רבן גמליאל's list: burning fats on the altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: The burning of fats, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה so it can discuss it. This is a setup line for the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, burning the fats and limbs of sacrifices on the altar is one of the things that may be done all night, until dawn. 'Etc.' signals that the full משנה line continues. Quoting it introduces the list the גמרא is about to examine.

keyTerms.meaning: burning (of sacrificial parts on the altar)
fats of a sacrifice that are burned on the altar
etc. (the quote continues)

phrases.english: The burning of fats, etc.
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה's list of מצוות that last until dawn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the discussion of the 'until חצות' wording to the specific items in the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Burning fats and limbs on the altar may be done until dawn.

steps.title: The Paschal lamb is missing from the list
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notices that eating the קרבן פסח is not listed among the מצוות that last until dawn.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the eating of the Paschal lamb is not taught in the list.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that eating the קרבן פסח is left out of the משנה's list. This is a setup observation that prepares the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קרבן פסח is also eaten at night, so we might expect it on the list. Its absence suggests its deadline is different and does not stretch until dawn. This leads into the question of how late the קרבן פסח may be eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: whereas, but (contrasts what is included with what is missing)
eating of the Paschal lamb (קרבן פסח)
it is not taught, it is not listed

phrases.english: Whereas the eating of the Paschal lambs is not taught.
phrases.notes: An inference from what the משנה left out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the list quoted in step 14 by noting what it omits.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The omission of eating the קרבן פסח implies that its deadline does not extend until dawn. This prepares a question on that point.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the פסח may be eaten until dawn
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that lists eating the פסח among the מצוות that last until dawn. This contradicts the משנה, which left it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא raises a contradiction: a ברייתא says that קריאת שמע at night, הלל on the nights of פסח, and eating the קרבן פסח may all be done until dawn!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא noticed that our משנה does not include eating the פסח in its list of מצוות that last until dawn. Now it brings a ברייתא that does include it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה left out eating the פסח. That suggests its deadline is earlier, at חצות. The ברייתא openly says it lasts until dawn, so the two sources seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction (one source against another)
הלל said on the nights of פסח
Eating the קרבן פסח
Dawn (first light)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a question about קריאת שמע. That part matches the משנה. The clash is only about eating the פסח.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction: the evening Shema,
and Hallel on the nights of Passover,
and eating the Paschal lamb,
their מצוה lasts until dawn rises!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 15's observation that the משנה omits eating the פסח, and sets a ברייתא against it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's implied view that eating the פסח does not last until dawn.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly lists eating the פסח as lasting until dawn, which contradicts the משנה's omission.

steps.title: רב יוסף: The two sources follow different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that the משנה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה and the ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: This is not difficult. This source follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, and that source follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף resolves the contradiction by saying the two sources reflect a disagreement between two תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף does not try to make the sources agree. He says they really do disagree, and each follows a different תנא. The משנה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, who says חצות. The ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא, who says dawn.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult
This one follows... that one follows...
A תנא who limits eating the פסח to חצות

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: It is not difficult:
this one follows Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya,
that one follows Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the sources to a מחלוקת תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא must agree, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: They follow different תנאים: the משנה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה (חצות), and the ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא (dawn).

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's source: 'this night' means until חצות
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי אלעזר בן עזריה compares 'this night' of eating the פסח to 'this night' of מכת בכורות, which happened at חצות.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'And they shall eat the meat on this night.' רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says: Here it says 'on this night,' and later it says, 'And I will pass through the land of מצרים on this night.' Just as there it means until חצות, so too here it means until חצות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that רבי אלעזר בן עזריה really holds the deadline is חצות, and to show his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses a גזירה שוה: the same words 'בלילה הזה' appear in two פסוקים. ה׳ struck the firstborn at חצות. So the eating, which uses the same words, also ends at חצות.

keyTerms.meaning: As a ברייתא teaches
It says here... and it says there (the form of a גזירה שוה)
Learning one פסוק from another because they share the same words
Just as there... so too here

steps.confusionAlert: The second פסוק does not mention חצות itself. We know מכת בכורות happened at חצות from another פסוק ('כחצות הלילה').

phrases.english: As it was taught: "And they shall eat the meat on this night,"
Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:
It says here "on this night,"
and it says further on:
"And I will pass through the land of Egypt on this night,"
just as there it is until midnight,
so too here it is until midnight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יוסף's claim by showing the source for רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's view.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's claim that רבי אלעזר בן עזריה limits eating the פסח to חצות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא showing his גזירה שוה from 'בלילה הזה' in the פסוק about מכת בכורות.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: The פסח is eaten until the time of haste
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא rejects the חצות limit. The פסוק says the פסח is eaten 'in haste,' so it lasts until the time of haste, which is dawn.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: Doesn't the פסוק already say 'in haste'? That means until the time of haste.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא pushes back against רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's חצות deadline by pointing to a different word in the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'haste' was when בני ישראל rushed out of מצרים. That happened in the morning, since they were told not to leave their houses until morning. So the פסח may be eaten until dawn. This is the view the ברייתא from Step 16 follows.

keyTerms.meaning: But hasn't it already been said?
In haste
The time of haste (the time of leaving מצרים, at dawn)

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him:
But has it not already been said "in haste"?
Meaning until the time of haste.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's גזירה שוה with a competing source.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the conclusion that eating the פסח ends at חצות.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word 'בחפזון' sets the deadline at the time of haste (dawn), so 'this night' cannot be the deciding word.

steps.title: Then why does the פסוק say 'at night'?
steps.stepSummary: Raising a question on רבי עקיבא's own view: if 'haste' sets the deadline, what does the word 'בלילה' teach?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the פסוק say 'at night'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא himself raises the obvious question on his own reading, and the next step gives his answer. If 'haste' gives the deadline, the word 'בלילה' seems to add nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word in the תורה must teach something. If רבי עקיבא does not use 'בלילה' for the deadline, he needs to explain what the word is there for.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
What does the פסוק come to teach?

phrases.english: If so, why does the verse say "at night"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions רבי עקיבא's view from Step 19 about the role of the word 'בלילה'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word 'בלילה' teaches according to רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: 'At night' teaches that the פסח is eaten at night, not by day
steps.stepSummary: The word 'בלילה' teaches that, unlike other קדשים, the פסח is eaten at night and not during the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think the פסח is eaten during the day like other קדשים. So the פסוק says 'at night': it is eaten at night and not during the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers that 'בלילה' teaches when the פסח is eaten (night, not day). It does not teach how late it may be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most קדשים are eaten during the day. Without 'בלילה,' we might have thought the פסח is the same. For רבי עקיבא, 'בלילה' sets the time of eating as night, while 'בחפזון' sets the end point at dawn.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought
Sacrifices (holy offerings)
And not during the day

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: 'בלילה הזה' means until חצות (from מכת בכורות). רבי עקיבא: 'בחפזון' means until dawn, and 'בלילה' only teaches that the פסח is eaten at night, not by day. Our משנה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, and the ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the contradiction from Step 16. The disagreement comes from which word in the פסוקים each תנא treats as setting the deadline.

phrases.english: One might think it is eaten during the day like other sacrifices;
therefore the verse says "at night":
at night it is eaten, and not during the day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'בלילה' teaches that the פסח is eaten at night and not by day, unlike other קדשים.

steps.title: What does רבי עקיבא learn from the word "this"?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה needs the word "הזה" for his גזירה שוה. For רבי עקיבא, who does not use that גזירה שוה, the word seems extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, who uses a גזירה שוה, that the תורה had to write "this" night. But according to רבי עקיבא, what does he learn from the word "this"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the word "בלילה" (handled in the last step) to the word "הזה". It asks what רבי עקיבא learns from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה uses "הַלַּיְלָה הַזֶּה" to link the night of eating the פסח to the night of מכת בכורות. That link is how he gets the חצות deadline. רבי עקיבא rejects that link, so the word "הזה" looks unused in his view, and the גמרא asks what it is for.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (introduces the side that has no problem)
A teaching that links two topics because the same word appears in both
It was necessary to write
What does he do with it? (What does he learn from this word?)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the last question. Steps 20–21 asked about the word "בלילה" (night). Now the גמרא is asking about a different word: "הזה" (this).

phrases.english: It makes sense according to Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya
who holds of the verbal analogy,
phrases.notes: Linking "this night" of the פסח to "this night" of מכת בכורות

phrases.english: the verse needed to write "this" for him.
But according to Rabbi Akiva,
what does he do with this word "this"?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה דְּאִית לֵיהּ גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the word "בלילה" for רבי עקיבא, the גמרא now asks about the next word in the same phrase, "הזה".
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does רבי עקיבא learn from the word "הזה", since he does not use it for the גזירה שוה?

steps.title: "This night" rules out eating the פסח on a second night
steps.stepSummary: "הזה" excludes a second night. Without it, we might compare the פסח to שלמים and say it is eaten for two nights and the day between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to exclude another night. You might have thought: the פסח is קדשים קלים, and שלמים are also קדשים קלים. Just as שלמים are eaten for two days and one night, the פסח should be eaten for two nights instead of two days, and so be eaten for two nights and one day. So the תורה teaches "on this night": on this night it is eaten, and not on another night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that for רבי עקיבא, the word "הזה" means only this one night, not a second night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both the פסח and שלמים are קדשים קלים, so we might think they get the same length of time to be eaten. שלמים get two days and the night between. Since the פסח is a nighttime offering, we might flip that to two nights and the day between. The word "הזה" blocks this and limits the פסח to one night only.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude
It would have entered your mind to say (the mistaken idea the פסוק comes to block)
Offerings of lesser holiness
Peace-offerings, eaten for two days and one night
So it teaches us

steps.confusionAlert: The mistaken idea is not "two nights and two days." It is a flipped version of the שלמים rule. שלמים have two days with one night between them. The פסח would have had two nights with one day between them.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains every word of "בַּלַּיְלָה הַזֶּה" for רבי עקיבא. "בלילה" means at night, not by day, and "הזה" means only one night.

phrases.english: It comes to exclude another night,
for it would have entered your mind to say:
since the Paschal offering is an offering of lesser holiness,
and peace-offerings are offerings of lesser holiness,

phrases.aramaic: מָה שְׁלָמִים נֶאֱכָלִין לִשְׁנֵי יָמִים וְלַיְלָה אֶחָד —
phrases.english: just as peace-offerings are eaten for two days and one night —
so too the Paschal offering is eaten for two nights
in place of two days,

phrases.aramaic: וִיהֵא נֶאֱכָל לִשְׁנֵי לֵילוֹת וְיוֹם אֶחָד.
phrases.english: and it would be eaten for two nights and one day.
So the verse teaches us "on this night":
on this night it is eaten,
and it is not eaten on another night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For רבי עקיבא, "הזה" excludes a second night. It blocks a comparison to שלמים that would have allowed two nights and a day.

steps.title: Then how does רבי אלעזר בן עזריה know there is no second night?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה uses "הזה" for his גזירה שוה. So where does he learn that the פסח is not eaten on a second night?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, from where does he learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the question around to the other side. It is setting up the next step, where we find his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה has already used the word "הזה" for his גזירה שוה. That means it is not free to also exclude a second night. Since he surely agrees the פסח is not eaten on a second night, he needs a different source.

keyTerms.meaning: And רבי אלעזר בן עזריה… (short form of the question "how does he know?")
From where does he learn it? (understood here, not written)
Another (second) night

steps.confusionAlert: This line is only a name, but it is a full question. The words "from where does he learn it?" are understood, not written.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya — from where does he learn this?
phrases.notes: The question "from where does he learn it?" is understood from context.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the same question to the other side of the dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Since רבי אלעזר בן עזריה uses "הזה" for his גזירה שוה, what is his source that the פסח is not eaten on a second night?

steps.title: He learns it from "Do not leave any until morning"
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה learns it from "לא תותירו עד בקר". If you may not leave the פסח until morning, you surely may not keep it until the next night.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from "You shall not leave any of it until morning."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's source. The פסוק "לא תותירו עד בקר" already shows there is no second night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה forbids leaving any of the פסח until the morning. So it is obvious that it cannot still be eaten the night after that, which is even later. This means רבי אלעזר בן עזריה does not need "הזה" to exclude a second night, and the word stays free for his גזירה שוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not leave over
Until morning
It comes out / is learned from

steps.whatToRemember: In "בַּלַּיְלָה הַזֶּה": for רבי עקיבא, "בלילה" means at night, not by day, and "הזה" means not a second night. For רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, "הזה" is used for the גזירה שוה with מכת בכורות, which gives the חצות deadline. He learns "no second night" from "לא תותירו עד בקר".

phrases.english: He derives it from "You shall not leave any of it until morning."
phrases.notes: Exodus 12:10. If it cannot be left until morning, it surely cannot be left until the next night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה learns that there is no second night from "לא תותירו עד בקר", so "הזה" stays free for his גזירה שוה.

steps.title: Why רבי עקיבא still needs the word הזה
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא cannot rely on לא תותירו עד בקר alone. Without הזה, we might think 'morning' means the second morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why doesn't רבי עקיבא learn it from לא תותירו עד בקר? If he learned it from there, I would have said: which 'morning' does the פסוק mean? The second morning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns back to רבי עקיבא. It explains why he cannot learn the 'no second night' rule from לא תותירו עד בקר, the way רבי אלעזר בן עזריה did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says not to leave the פסח 'until morning', but it does not say which morning. Someone could think it means the morning after a second night, the way שלמים may be eaten for two days. So רבי עקיבא needs the extra word הזה ('this night') to close off that possibility.

keyTerms.meaning: If [we learned it] from there, meaning from the other פסוק
I would have said (a mistaken first thought)
The second morning

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva — if [he learned it] from there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the פסוק לא תותירו עד בקר from step 25.

phrases.english: I would have said: what is 'morning'?
The second morning.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא — אִי מֵהָתָם, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the unspoken question: if רבי אלעזר בן עזריה can learn the rule from לא תותירו עד בקר, why can't רבי עקיבא?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why doesn't רבי עקיבא learn the 'no second night' rule from לא תותירו עד בקר?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because 'morning' alone could mean the second morning, so the extra word הזה is needed.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: 'morning' always means the first morning
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה answers that an unexplained 'morning' in the תורה always means the very next morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר would tell you: every 'morning' in the תורה means the first morning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's reply to the worry raised for רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says the worry is not real. When the תורה says 'morning' without saying which one, it means the next morning. So לא תותירו עד בקר is already clear on its own, and he is free to use הזה for his גזירה שוה.

keyTerms.meaning: He would say to you (his reply)
The first morning, meaning the very next morning

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar would say to you:
phrases.notes: This is רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

phrases.english: Every 'morning' is the first morning.

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree there is no second night for the פסח. They only disagree about which פסוק teaches it. רבי עקיבא learns it from הזה. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה learns it from לא תותירו עד בקר, because 'morning' always means the next morning.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי אלעזר בן עזריה against the worry raised in step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A rule of reading: an unexplained 'morning' means the first morning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Morning' might mean the second morning, so another word would be needed to rule out a second night.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Morning' always means the next morning, so לא תותירו עד בקר is enough.

steps.title: The same argument appears between earlier תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the argument between רבי עקיבא and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה matches an argument in a ברייתא. It quotes the פסוק they argue about.
steps.simpleTranslation: These תנאים argue like those תנאים. As a ברייתא teaches about the פסוק: 'There you shall slaughter the פסח in the evening, as the sun sets, at the time you went out of מצרים.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new point: this same argument also appears between other תנאים. This line sets things up by quoting the פסוק. The next steps show the two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names three times: 'in the evening', 'as the sun sets', and 'the time you went out of מצרים'. Each תנא will explain these three times differently. That difference will match the question of until when the פסח may be eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: These תנאים are like those תנאים (they argue about the same issue)
As a ברייתא teaches
The time you went out of מצרים

phrases.english: And these tannaim are like those tannaim.
As it was taught [in a baraita]:
"There you shall slaughter the Pesach
phrases.notes: דברים טז:ו

phrases.english: in the evening, as the sun sets,
at the time you went out of Egypt."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back from the details and links the whole argument to a second pair of תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument between רבי עקיבא and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה matches an argument in a ברייתא about this פסוק.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: three times for slaughtering, eating, and burning
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר reads the three times in the פסוק as three stages: slaughtering, eating, and burning what is left over.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: 'In the evening' you slaughter. 'As the sun sets' you eat. 'At the time you went out of מצרים' you burn.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the first opinion. רבי אליעזר gives each time in the פסוק its own job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אליעזר, the 'time you went out of מצרים' is no longer eating time. By then, any meat still left is נותר and must be burned. The eating time ends earlier, at midnight. This matches רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughter the offering
Eat
Burn (the leftover meat)
Meat of a קרבן left past its time, which must be burned

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
'In the evening' you slaughter,
phrases.notes: The afternoon of the 14th of ניסן.

phrases.english: and 'as the sun sets' you eat,
and 'at the time you went out of Egypt' you burn.
phrases.notes: By this time eating is over, and leftovers must be burned.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבי אליעזר (in this ברייתא) with רבי אלעזר בן עזריה (from the earlier steps). They are different people, though they hold the same view: eating ends at midnight.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first opinion in the ברייתא introduced in step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughter in the afternoon, eat from sunset, and burn the leftovers at the time of going out of מצרים. Eating does not continue until then. This matches רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: you may keep eating until the time of going out
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע says the 'time you went out of מצרים' is when eating ends, not a separate time for burning. This matches רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: 'In the evening' you slaughter. 'As the sun sets' you eat. And until when may you keep eating? Until 'the time you went out of מצרים'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the second opinion. רבי יהושע uses the last time in the פסוק as the end of the eating time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר made the last time into a burning time. רבי יהושע instead makes it the end of eating. The going out of מצרים was in the morning, so for him the פסח may be eaten all night until morning, just like רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Until when?
Keep on eating

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
'In the evening' you slaughter,
'as the sun sets' you eat,
and until when do you keep on eating?
Until 'the time you went out of Egypt.'
phrases.notes: Meaning the morning, when בני ישראל left.

steps.whatToRemember: The two arguments line up. רבי אליעזר agrees with רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: eat until midnight. רבי יהושע agrees with רבי עקיבא: eat until morning.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רב יוסף's answer in step 17 is not an isolated idea. The same disagreement about eating the פסח (midnight or morning) already appears between earlier תנאים, and our משנה, which leaves the פסח off its dawn list, follows the midnight side.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second opinion in the ברייתא, disagreeing with רבי אליעזר in step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסח may be eaten from sunset until the time of going out of מצרים, which is morning. This matches רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: Everyone agrees: redeemed at night, left by day
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא says that both sides agree. The גאולה happened at night, and the actual leaving from מצרים happened during the day. Each point has its own פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: Everyone agrees that when ישראל were redeemed from מצרים, they were redeemed only in the evening, as it says: 'ה׳ your God took you out of מצרים at night.' And when they actually left, they left only during the day, as it says: 'On the day after the פסח, בני ישראל went out with a high hand.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא starts a new way of explaining the argument between רבי אלעזר בן עזריה and רבי עקיבא. First he sets out the facts that both sides agree on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two פסוקים seem to contradict each other: one says 'at night' and one says 'the day after.' רבי אבא settles this by separating two events. The גאולה (getting permission to leave) happened at night, and the actual walking out happened by day. Since both sides accept this, the argument must be about something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
They were redeemed (freed from slavery)
They went out (physically left)
On the day after the פסח
With a high hand: openly and proudly

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'נגאלו' (being redeemed) with 'יצאו' (leaving). רבי אבא's whole point is that these are two different events at two different times.
steps.whyThisMatters: This narrows the argument between רבי אלעזר בן עזריה and רבי עקיבא. Since both agree on when the גאולה happened and when they left, their argument cannot be about those facts. רבי אבא himself names the real issue in the next step: whose 'haste' the פסוק means.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said:
Everyone agrees that when Israel were redeemed from Egypt,
they were redeemed only in the evening,
phrases.notes: This means they were given permission to leave that night.

phrases.english: as it says: 'The Lord your God took you out of Egypt at night,'
phrases.notes: From דברים ט״ז:א׳.

phrases.english: and when they actually left, they left only during the day,
as it says: 'On the day after the Passover offering,'
'the Children of Israel went out with a high hand.'
phrases.notes: From במדבר ל״ג:ג׳.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the argument between רבי אלעזר בן עזריה and רבי עקיבא from steps 17–21 and offers another way of framing it. It first sets out the facts both sides agree on, and then names the real point of dispute: the meaning of 'חפזון'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both sides agree: the גאולה happened at night, and the physical leaving happened by day.

steps.title: The real argument is about 'haste' and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's view
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא says the argument is about the 'time of haste.' רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says the haste means the Egyptians' haste.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what did they argue? About the time of haste. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה held: What is 'haste'? The haste of the Egyptians.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא now names the real point of argument: the word 'חפזון' in the פסוק about eating the קרבן פסח. Then he gives רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says to eat the קרבן פסח 'בחפזון,' in haste. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says this means the Egyptians' rush at midnight to send the Jews out during מכת בכורות. So the eating time lasts only until midnight.

keyTerms.meaning: About what did they argue?
The time of haste
Held, was of the opinion
The haste of the Egyptians

phrases.english: About what did they argue?
phrases.notes: This is a rhetorical question by רבי אבא. It is not a challenge.

phrases.english: About the time of haste,
phrases.notes: This refers to שמות י״ב:י״א: 'You shall eat it in haste.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya held:
What is 'haste'? The haste of Egypt.
phrases.notes: The Egyptians rushed at midnight, during מכת בכורות, to send the Jews away.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל מָה נֶחְלְקוּ — עַל שְׁעַת חִפָּזוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After ruling out time of leaving as the issue, it names the true point of argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument is about 'חפזון.' רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says it means the Egyptians' midnight haste, so the eating time ends at midnight.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's view: it is the Jews' haste
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says 'חפזון' means the haste of the Jews as they rushed out of מצרים in the morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא held: What is 'haste'? The haste of ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the other side of the argument. רבי עקיבא explains 'חפזון' differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, the haste is the Jews hurrying out of מצרים in the morning. So the time for eating the קרבן פסח stretches until dawn. This matches his view that it may be eaten all night.

keyTerms.meaning: The haste of the Jewish people (in the morning)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אבא, both sides agree on the night and day facts. The argument is only about whose haste the פסוק means. If it is the Egyptians' haste, the eating time ends at midnight (רבי אלעזר בן עזריה). If it is the Jews' haste, the eating time ends at dawn (רבי עקיבא).

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva held:
What is 'haste'? The haste of Israel.
phrases.notes: The Jews rushed to leave in the morning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided explanation begun in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא says 'חפזון' is the Jews' morning haste, so the eating time ends at dawn.

steps.title: A ברייתא asks: did they really leave at night?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רבי אבא. It starts by pointing out the clash between the 'at night' פסוק and the 'by day' פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: 'ה׳ your God took you out of מצרים at night.' Did they leave at night? Didn't they leave only during the day, as it says: 'On the day after the פסח, בני ישראל went out with a high hand'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up רבי אבא. This step is the ברייתא's question, and it sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא raises the same contradiction that רבי אבא solved: one פסוק says 'at night' and another says 'by day.' Raising this question prepares the ground for the same solution רבי אבא gave.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (in a ברייתא), bringing support
Is it really so? Introduces a question of surprise
But isn't it so that...?

phrases.english: It was also taught so (in a baraita):
'The Lord your God took you out of Egypt at night':
Did they really leave at night?
But didn't they leave only during the day,
as it says: 'On the day after the Passover offering'
'the Children of Israel went out with a high hand'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support רבי אבא's division between night and day.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אבא's claim that the גאולה was at night while the leaving was by day.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on the פסוק 'הוציאך ה׳ אלהיך ממצרים לילה.'

steps.title: The ברייתא's answer: the גאולה began at night
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers that 'at night' teaches that the גאולה began in the evening, even though the leaving was by day. This matches רבי אבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it teaches that the גאולה began for them in the evening.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא resolves its own question. That answer is exactly רבי אבא's point, so the support is now complete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'At night' does not mean they walked out at night. It means the גאולה started at night. This is the same split רבי אבא made between being redeemed and leaving, so the ברייתא confirms his reading.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches
The redemption began for them

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא confirms רבי אבא: the גאולה began at night, and the actual leaving happened by day.

phrases.english: Rather, it teaches
that the redemption began for them in the evening.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהִתְחִילָה לָהֶם גְּאוּלָּה מִבָּעֶרֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's question from the previous step, completing the support for רבי אבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the פסוק: 'at night' refers to the start of the גאולה, not to the physical leaving.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'At night' means they physically left at night, which would clash with the 'by day' פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גאולה began at night, and the leaving happened by day.

steps.title: The word נא means 'please'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק 'דבר נא באזני העם.' The school of רבי ינאי says the word נא always means 'please.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Speak, please (נא), in the ears of the people.' The students of רבי ינאי said: 'נא' is nothing but a way of asking nicely.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new piece of אגדה about leaving מצרים. It quotes a פסוק and explains the meaning of one word in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ is giving a command to משה, so it is strange to find the word נא, which means 'please,' in it. The school of רבי ינאי says this word is a real request and not just filler. This sets up the question of why ה׳ would need to ask nicely, which the next step answers.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Speak, please.' The opening words of the פסוק (שמות יא:ב)
'They said.' Used when a group, such as a school of students, makes a statement
The house of study (students) of רבי ינאי
A way of asking, a polite request
'Is nothing but.' A phrase that gives the one and only meaning of a word

steps.confusionAlert: Don't connect this to the argument in the steps before. The גמרא is not still debating night versus day. It is starting a new, related אגדה about leaving מצרים.

phrases.english: "Speak, please, in the ears of the people," etc.
phrases.notes: שמות יא:ב. The rest of the פסוק tells them to borrow silver and gold vessels.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yannai said:
"Na" is nothing but an expression of request (please),

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי דְּבֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי: אֵין נָא אֶלָּא לְשׁוֹן בַּקָּשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The topic is connected because both are about leaving מצרים, but this opens a new אגדה and does not continue the night/day debate.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word נא in a פסוק means a sincere request: 'please.'

steps.title: ה׳ asks משה to ask the people to borrow vessels
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא says 'please' to משה, and tells him to say 'please' to ישראל and ask them to borrow silver and gold vessels from מצרים. The reason begins with 'so that... should not say,' and continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא said to משה: 'Please, I ask you, go and tell ישראל: Please, I ask you, borrow silver vessels and gold vessels from the Egyptians, so that... should not say...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the 'please' works in the story: ה׳ is asking very politely for the people to take wealth from מצרים. The last words, 'so that... should not say,' open a reason that continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two layers of 'please.' ה׳ asks משה, and משה is to ask the people. That shows ה׳ really wanted this done, even though the people only wanted to get out. The reason is cut off here. It explains that ה׳'s promise to אברהם at the ברית בין הבתרים, that his children would leave with great wealth, must be kept.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, Blessed be He (ה׳)
'I ask of you, please.' A polite request
Borrow, or ask for (vessels)
Vessels of silver and vessels of gold
'So that [someone] should not say.' Introduces the reason

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how much ה׳ cared about keeping His word to אברהם, so much that He asked politely for it to be fulfilled.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לֵיהּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Moses:

phrases.aramaic: בְּבַקָּשָׁה מִמְּךָ, לֵךְ וֶאֱמוֹר לָהֶם לְיִשְׂרָאֵל:
phrases.english: I ask of you, please, go and tell Israel:
I ask of you, please, borrow from the Egyptians
vessels of silver and vessels of gold,
so that ... should not say
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next עמוד. It goes on to say 'that righteous one' (אברהם) should not complain that the promise was not kept.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה: בְּבַקָּשָׁה מִמְּךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the explanation that נא means 'please' and shows the 'please' being said inside the story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ politely asked, through משה, that ישראל borrow silver and gold from the Egyptians. The reason continues on the next עמוד.
